title: Emergent behavior reading notes + quick experiments
content:
Quick brain dump after reading a few recent posts/papers about emergent abilities in LLMs + sketch of lightweight experiments we can run on Redwood. Mostly for personal reference; will turn into a small PR with notebook and eval set if results look interesting.

High-level takeaway (TL;DR):
- "Emergent" usually means non-linear capability scaling: capabilities that are absent below a threshold and appear rapidly as model size or data changes.
- Mechanisms are unsettled: hypothesis space includes increased feature reuse, sparse computation of latent heuristics, and phase transitions in attention dynamics.
- Practical implication for serving: small model variants may fail silently on workloads that require those emergent skills; fallback policies and evals need coverage for sharp capability cliffs.

Notes on specific reads (quick bullets):
- "Emergent Abilities of LLMs" (survey/blog) — argues for systematic capability maps by task. Key point: coarse benchmarks miss localized task cliffs (e.g., multi-step reasoning vs single-step QA).
- "Scaling and Phase Transitions" (conference paper notes) — experiments showing discrete jumps in token prediction accuracy on synthetic tasks as param count passes thresholds. Interesting experimental design: synthetic task families that isolate compositional generalization.
- Follow-up blog: causal probing suggests some emergent features correspond to learned subroutines reused across tasks (not just bigger memorization).

Immediate questions for Redwood context:
1) Which production endpoints are most at risk of emergent cliffs? My initial list: code generation, multi-turn summarization, instruction-following with nested conditionals.
2) How do we detect capability cliffs automatically from logs? Candidate signals: sudden spike in error rate for specific prompt templates, increased latency with repeated retries, or divergence in embedding similarity between prompt+response pairs.
3) Can we craft a tiny probe benchmark (10–20 examples per capability) for rollout/monitoring to catch regressions across model variants? Should be synthetic + real prompts.

Small experiment plan (can run on hosted API + local runner):
- Experiment A: Threshold sweep across model sizes (tiny -> base -> large) on a small chain-of-thought style task family (e.g., 3-step arithmetic, nested conditionals). Measure pass@1 accuracy and instability.
- Experiment B: Ablation of few-shot examples (0/1/3/5) to see if capability onset shifts with context.
- Experiment C: Evaluate fallback policies: route to cheaper model, then to larger one. Track user-visible metrics (latency, correctness) and cost.

Metrics to collect (practical):
- pass_rate_by_prompt_template (per-template accuracy) — easier to compute than full evals.
- response_confidence proxies: logprob gaps, next-token entropy, repetition rates.
- retry_count_distribution — if capability cliffs cause more retries.

Prototype checklist (low friction):
- [ ] Build a 40-example probe suite covering: multi-step arithmetic, multi-hop commonsense, nested instructions, instruction tuning edge cases (negation, conditional logic).
- [ ] Notebook that runs sweep across 4 model sizes and records per-prompt pass/fail + logprobs.
- [ ] Lightweight dashboard in console (per-probe charts) + slack alert if pass_rate drops > 10% vs baseline.

Potential pitfalls / things to watch:
- Small sample sizes can give noisy cliffs; need to estimate significance (bootstrap).
- Few-shot prompting can hide or reveal capabilities; probe design must control for demonstration effects.
- Quantized / distilled variants: emergence may shift unpredictably (not strictly monotonic).

Ideas for Redwood product implications (brainstorm):
- Canary probe sets: when rolling a new model, run the 40-probe suite as part of rollout gating. If a probe drops, trigger automatic rollback or restrict the route.
- Capability metadata: tag model variants with flags (e.g., "strong-chain-of-thought", "weak-nested-conditions") derived from probe results. Use these in routing policies.
- Auto-fallback heuristics: if model returns low-confidence/low-logprob output on certain templates, route to a specialized variant.

Links / artifacts to follow up (scratch):
- arXiv/blog: emergent abilities survey (read 2023–2025 lit) — saved in reading queue.
- internal slack thread: #research-emergence (recent convo with Aisha and Marco).
- GH: small-probes repo idea (will open PR adding 40-probe suite).

To-dos (if I get time this week):
- Turn the 40-example probe into a JSONL + simple runner that hits hosted API + local Kubernetes runner for dedicated clusters.
- Draft a short doc for product: "Canary probe checklist for model rollouts" (one pager).

Open questions / unresolved:
- How many capabilities are "real" emergent vs just under-evaluated? Need variance analysis.
- Do distillation/quantization processes create new emergent cliffs? (Probably yes — need to test.)

Notes to self:
- Keep probes small & interpretable; product folks prefer simple pass/fail checks.
- Tag each probe with explicit rubric (what counts as pass).
- Share early with Aisha (applied-ml) and Priya (prod) for feedback on what matters for SLAs.

End notes: This doc is messy, intentionally. Next step: implement Experiment A and push notebook to GH under 'rls/probes/emergetest' and add link here.
